editorial.headline: Can AI Help Scientists Read the Moon?
editorial.hook: NASA and IBM released a new AI tool for Moon science. It helps researchers work with huge amounts of lunar data.
editorial.quick_summary: NASA and IBM released an open-source AI model for lunar science. It can help researchers map craters, study volcanic features, and estimate places where ice may be stable near the Moon's poles.

sections.title: What did NASA and IBM release?
sections.text: The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model is an open-source AI model for Moon research. NASA says it was trained mainly on Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data, including roughly two million image tiles from years of observations.

checkpoint.prompt: What is the model mainly designed to help scientists do?
choices: Analyze large amounts of lunar data
Move the Moon closer to Earth
checkpoint.answer: Analyze large amounts of lunar data
checkpoint.explanation: The model is a research tool for working with Moon data.

sections.title: What can the model help study?
sections.text: Researchers can adapt the model to map craters, spot unusual volcanic features, and estimate where ice may be stable near the Moon's poles. That word estimate matters: the model can point to promising places, but a prediction is not the same as direct proof of ice.

checkpoint.prompt: Stop & Check: Does 'estimate where ice may exist' mean 'prove ice is there'?
checkpoint.explanation: An estimate is evidence-based, but it is not the same as direct confirmation.

sections.title: Extension: What does 'open-source' change?
sections.text: NASA and IBM made the model publicly available so researchers can test, adapt, and compare it. They also released machine-learning-ready data and benchmark materials. This can make it easier for research teams to build on the same tools instead of starting from zero.

basic.prompt: Find the fact: Name one lunar feature the model can help scientists study.
basic.answer: Examples include craters, volcanic features, or possible stable ice areas near the poles.

standard.prompt: Why is the word 'estimate' important in this article?
standard.answer: Because the model can suggest likely locations, but its output is not direct proof that ice is present.

challenge.prompt: Which headline goes too far? A. AI model helps researchers study Moon data. B. AI proves where water ice is hidden on the Moon.
challenge.answer: B goes too far. The sources say the model can estimate where ice may be stable, not prove ice at every location.

rescue.hint_1: First find the main subject and verb: 'The model ... can help ...'
rescue.hint_2: Watch evidence words such as can, may, and estimate. They show that a claim is limited.
rescue.summary: Main idea: NASA and IBM made an AI tool that helps scientists work with large Moon datasets, but its predictions still need scientific interpretation.

key_words.example: The model can help map craters.
The model can estimate where ice may be stable.
Researchers can test the open-source model.

language_support.focus_sentence: Because the model is already trained on lunar data, scientists can adapt it to map craters and estimate where ice may be stable.

sentence_breakdown.Because: the model is already trained on lunar data
sentence_breakdown.For what: map craters; estimate stable ice areas

language_support.zh_rescue_summary: NASA與IBM發布一個用於月球科學的開源AI模型。它主要利用多年累積的月球觀測資料，協助研究者繪製隕石坑、辨識火山特徵，並推估月球極區哪些地方可能適合冰長期存在。重點是：推估不等於直接證明，AI仍是科學家的工具。

uncertainties: The 23% figure applies to benchmark comparisons on some tasks, not every possible Moon-science task.
Ice estimates are model outputs and should not be described as direct confirmation.

exam_connection.note: Possible questions: main idea, meaning of 'estimate', what 'open-source' changes, or whether a headline claims more than the evidence supports.
